summary: Georg Morgenstierne worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Oslo (ca. 1909–1914) and under Sten Konow (ca. 1918–1921), later holding a post at the University of Gothenburg (ca. 1930–1937).

Georg Wilhelm Freytag worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen (ca. 1807–1811) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (ca. 1815–1819), holding posts at Göttingen (ca. 1811–1815) and the University of Bonn (ca. 1819–1861).

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as verantwortlicher Redaktor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968) and held a professorship at the University of Oslo (ca. 1977–2003).

Georg von der Gabelentz was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena (ca. 1858–1860) and Leipzig University (ca. 1860–1864), later holding posts at Leipzig (1878) and Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1889–1893).

George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UCSB and UCLA, working under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and other faculty, before holding posts at CU Boulder (ca. 2004–2007) and the University of Saskatchewan (ca. 2011).

George Abraham Grierson worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at St. Bees School (ca. 1864–1868) and Trinity College Dublin (ca. 1868–1871), later serving in the Indian Civil Service (ca. 1871–1898) and at the Asiatic Society (ca. 1894–1897).

George Baumann is an Indologist who completed his PhD at Heidelberg University in 1973. He served as director of the Oriental Department at the University of Tübingen (ca. 1974–2000) and at the Tübingen University Library (1976–2001).
George C. O. Haas was a scholar of Indology. He served as editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society and held the post of Recording Secretary at the American Oriental Society.

George Cardona worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at New York University (ca. 1953–1956) and Yale University (ca. 1957–1960), held a fellowship at CASBS (1971–1972), and was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (ca. 1965–2006).

George Chemparathy specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner (ca. 1964–1969) and Paul Hacker, and held academic posts at Loyola College, Chennai (ca. 1957–1961) and Utrecht University (ca. 1975–1993).
George Cœdès was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (ca. 1904–1906) and served as president of the Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD from Northwestern University (ca. 1968–1972), where he later served as Professor of Religion (ca. 1974–2012).

George Foot Moore worked in religious studies. He studied at Yale University (ca. 1868–1872) and held professorships at Andover Theological Seminary (ca. 1883–1902) and Harvard University (ca. 1902–1928).

George J. Tanabe, Jr. is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under committee member Jørn Borup and served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (ca. 1977–2006).

George L. Hart specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Harvard University (ca. 1960–1969) and held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1969–1975) and the University of California, Berkeley (ca. 1975–2013).

George Lakoff is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (ca. 1958–1962) and Indiana University (ca. 1962–1966), later holding a post at the University of California, Berkeley (ca. 1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Loyola University Maryland (ca. 1887–1891) and Johns Hopkins University (ca. 1891–1896), later holding posts at Catholic University of America, Johns Hopkins, and Ohio State University (1914–1939).

George Peiris Malalasekera worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, he held posts at Ananda, Nalanda, Ceylon University College, and the University of Ceylon.
George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his studies at Columbia University in 1978 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

George Roerich specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Karl May School, University of London under Lobsang Mingyur Dorje, and Harvard, later heading the philosophy department at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies.
